title: Diaphragm Skeletal Muscle Preparation
author: Sunamita Lima
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.p7vdrn6
materials: The animal was euthanized by cervical dislocation

steps.title: Prepare Tyrode's solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve the following in distilled water: 11 g D‑glucose, 135 mM NaCl, 5 mM KCl, 0 mM MgCl₂·6H₂O, 2 mM CaCl₂, 0 mM Na₂HPO₄·H₂O, 1 mM NaHCO₃; adjust to final volume and keep at room temperature.

steps.title: Dissect diaphragm muscle
steps.instruction: Remove the diaphragm muscle from the animal and immediately transfer it to a petri dish containing the prepared Tyrode’s solution.

steps.title: Trim to 1.5 cm segment
steps.instruction: Cut a 1.5 cm segment of diaphragm that includes the central tendon and the attached ribs.

steps.title: Mount preparation in organ bath
steps.instruction: Place the rib end onto a holder fixed at the bottom of an organ bath containing 5 mL of Tyrode’s solution; gently pin it in place. Attach the central tendon portion to a PowerLab force transducer. Maintain the bath at 30 °C and continuously bubble with 95 % O₂ / 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Rinse and incubate with blocker
steps.instruction: Rinse the tissue four times with fresh Tyrode’s solution, then incubate it in Tyrode’s containing 1 µM d‑tubocurarine.

steps.title: Stabilize and set optimal length
steps.instruction: Allow the preparation to stabilize for 20–30 min. After stabilization, readjust muscle length to achieve optimal twitch tension. Wait an additional 30 min before testing drug effects.

steps.title: Apply electrical stimulation
steps.instruction: Stimulate the muscle strips isometrically through silver electrodes using a supramaximal voltage, 0.1 Hz frequency, and 2 ms pulse duration.

steps.title: Assess drug effects
steps.instruction: After the 30‑minute post‑adjustment period, introduce test drugs and record their effects on twitch tension.
